facts.human_intro:
A reference at the end of a sentence can make unfinished research look finished. The paper might be real. The quoted sentence might be real too. Neither fact tells us whether someone opened the right version, read beyond the abstract or checked that the passage supports the conclusion.

QuoteLedger gives that unfinished work a place to live. A research lead stays a lead until its record contains more. You can retain a text snapshot, locate the passage you intend to quote and check that the recorded bytes and exact passage still match. If a human reviews the claim, that judgment is tied to the claim and source records they inspected.

Imagine a fictional report that says eight specimens took twelve minutes in one trial. Turning that into “the method always finishes every job in twelve minutes” changes the meaning. QuoteLedger can show that the quotation is intact and the review is current. It cannot make that leap in meaning valid. The package includes this deliberately wrong example so that a successful check is never confused with proof.

The useful distinction is between a link, an exact local quotation, a source declared primary and full text, and a completed review. Those are different records, not increasing confidence scores. An abstract can remain useful without being mislabeled as a full-text check. A changed claim can keep its source while losing the applicability of an old review.

The small Python tool runs locally without a model or network connection. Its CSV intake preserves original bytes and extra columns rather than throwing away context. It can prepare pending review records and produce JSON or a readable report. It does not rewrite the original packet, fetch papers or approve research on your behalf.

The accompanying working paper explains the contract and its limits. The recorded release passed 67 unit tests, matched 20 authored cases and 64 generated checks, and passed ten packaging checks. These are synthetic implementation checks, not a measurement of better real-world citations.

The goal is modest and practical: make it easier to see what has actually been checked and what still deserves a person's attention. The structured companion keeps the detailed records available without making this introduction read like a database.

facts.definition: A supplied assertion awaiting source inspection; a link is not a record of reading.
Exact local UTF-8 bytes identified by a SHA-256. This does not authenticate the publisher or the original PDF.
A matching raw snapshot digest and an identical Unicode-code-point span, without normalization.
A supplied description such as full text, abstract, snippet or summary. QuoteLedger does not infer or authenticate it.
An explicit completed or pending decision whose binding covers the claim and cited source metadata; not an authenticated signature.
Agreement with the stated inspection rules, distinct from truth, entailment and authentic review.

facts.question: Can QuoteLedger verify that a cited paper exists?

nodes.label: Can QuoteLedger verify that a cited paper exists?

facts.answer: No. It does not query publishers, search engines, DOI registries or other external services. Source identity and URLs remain supplied assertions.

facts.question: Does a matching quotation prove the claim?

nodes.label: Does a matching quotation prove the claim?

facts.answer: No. A literal quote may be irrelevant or used to support an unjustified generalization. The false-but-consistent example makes this limitation explicit.

facts.question: Can an abstract count as primary full-text evidence?

nodes.label: Can an abstract count as primary full-text evidence?

facts.answer: An exact abstract quote can reach local_quote. It does not reach primary_quote under an honest abstract extent label. The software cannot detect a falsely supplied full_text label.

facts.question: Can I bring a research-tool or Elicit CSV into QuoteLedger?

nodes.label: Can I bring a research-tool or Elicit CSV into QuoteLedger?

facts.answer: You can map a CSV with claim, title and URL columns using configurable headers. The original bytes and extra columns are preserved. No native Elicit API integration or exhaustive export-format compatibility is claimed.

facts.question: What changes make a review stale?

nodes.label: What changes make a review stale?

facts.answer: Changing claim text, citations, declared basis or cited source metadata changes the claim binding. Review fields themselves are editable and are not authenticated.

facts.question: Does the tool send private research to a model?

facts.answer: The supplied tool performs no model or network calls. It reads local declared files when asked. Imported CSV records may still contain private information and must be reviewed before sharing.

facts.question: Is QuoteLedger a general anti-hallucination solution?

nodes.label: Is QuoteLedger a general anti-hallucination solution?

facts.answer: No. It is a bounded local record inspector. It can expose missing evidence conditions, changed snapshots and stale bindings, but it cannot determine semantic truth or discover claims omitted from the packet.
